title: Timing of nutrient input pulses during ice cover regulates lake spring plankton dynamics
content:
Abstract
Rising winter temperatures can increase rain and snowmelt events, which in turn can shift the timing of nutrient runoff earlier into the winter season. Nutrients entering lakes with runoff below ice are often assumed to stay in the water column until phytoplankton growth increases in spring following increased light availability. However, bacteria are rarely limited by light, and the mismatch between winter nutrient inputs and light availability can increase lake heterotrophy following increased bacterial growth. Here, we conducted a mesocosm experiment in a mesotrophic lake (Erken, Sweden) to test the effect of nutrient input timing below ice cover across trophic levels from bacteria to zooplankton. We added inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus on two occasions during ice cover to mimic an early and a late runoff event. Bacteria assimilated nutrients independent of when they were added, whereas phytoplankton chlorophyll a concentrations were significantly higher in the late runoff scenario, likely due to a combination of sufficient light and nutrient availability. Mixotrophs increased in the early runoff scenario, likely reflecting increased nutrient availability at times of light limitation. Our findings suggest that earlier winter runoff following thaw events may result in a comparably lower spring phytoplankton bloom through changes in the timing of nutrient and light availability.

title: A segmented-breakpoint measure of cross-shore sea-surface-temperature structure in the Benguela system
content:
A segmented-breakpoint measure of cross-shore sea-surface-temperature structure in the Benguela system
Albertus J. Smit and Neville A. Sweijd
Ocean Sci., 22, 3795–3809, https://doi.org/10.5194/os-22-3795-2026, 2026
We fit a daily breakpoint to cross-shore sea-surface-temperature profiles in five Benguela upwelling cells. Conventional 50 to 100 km offshore references usually sample inside the fitted cool tongue, which can weaken or reverse fixed-distance contrasts. The method clarifies how index definition shapes cell-scale comparisons and sea-surface-temperature and wind agreement.

title: Real-world longitudinal multi-omics separates weight-loss-associated responses to incretin agonists from a broader response not dependent on weight loss
content: The benefits of incretin agonists, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, are largely attributed to glycemic control and weight loss, as these therapies enhance insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release and delay gastric emptying to produce satiety. Yet treatment is also associated with lower risk of cardiometabolic, renal and other chronic diseases. Whether these broader benefits depend on weight loss itself or reflect direct effects of treatment on physiology remains unclear, as does the basis of the marked variation in how patients respond. Resolving these questions has been difficult because weight loss and drug effects occur together, and because molecular studies of treated patients have been limited in scope. Here we profiled paired plasma samples collected before and after treatment from 165 individuals drawn from DynamiQ, a biorepository that links plasma samples to longitudinal clinical records, combining mass spectrometry-based proteomics, a targeted inflammation proteomics panel (NULISAseq) and non-targeted metabolomics to capture metabolic function, inflammation and markers of chronic disease. Treatment was associated with broad remodeling of the plasma proteome and metabolome, but the extent to which this remodeling depended on weight loss differed across the molecular layers. The metabolome carried a lipid signature that scaled with the weight lost, whereas proteomic and inflammation-panel changes largely did not depend on weight loss. Among these changes, treatment was associated with lower circulating mitochondrial oxidative proteins and cardiolipins, consistent with relief of lipid-driven metabolic stress, and with a shift of the inflammation panel toward a less inflamed state. A metabolic aging clock showed that age acceleration decreased by a mean of 2.96 years after treatment (95% confidence interval -4.95 to -0.98; P = 3.7 x 10-3), a change that did not depend on weight loss or on the interval between samples, with the largest reductions in participants starting from the highest age acceleration, most of whom had diabetes. Treatment-associated features overlapped with features associated with cardiometabolic, renal and hepatic disease. Before treatment, higher systemic inflammation, reflecting chronic tissue stress and repair, was associated with less subsequent weight loss. Together, these findings indicate that incretin agonist treatment is associated with lower markers of metabolic and inflammatory stress and with a younger metabolic age, changes that do not depend on weight loss, identify baseline inflammation as an axis of heterogeneity in treatment response, and suggest that biorepositories linking longitudinal multi-omic profiling to clinical records can relate drug pharmacodynamics to disease risk and to variation in patient response.

title: Poxvirus-induced concurrent activation of SAMD9 and ERK establishes a unique immune state with heightened IFN-I responses to danger signals
content: Mammalian poxviruses must overcome the cellular restriction factor SAMD9 to establish productive infection. SAMD9 is a widely expressed cytoplasmic sensor of double-stranded nucleic acids (dsNA) that induces type-1 interferon (IFN-I) responses and possesses anticodon-nuclease activity targeting tRNAphe specifically. To counteract SAMD9, poxviruses have evolved dedicated antagonists, including myxoma virus (MYXV) M062, which blocks both dsNA sensing and tRNAphe-nuclease activity. However, the significance of tRNAphe depletion during poxvirus infection has remained unclear. Here, we showed that mammalian poxviruses exhibit an unexpected enrichment of phenylalanine within their proteomes and preferentially utilize UUU phenylalanine codon. In contrast, host interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) have lower phenylalanine frequencies than poxviruses and instead preferentially utilize UUC codon. Together with the known preferentially translational impairment of UUU-rich transcripts following SAMD9-mediated tRNAphe depletion, these findings suggest a mechanism by which unobstructed SAMD9 disproportionally restricts poxvirus protein synthesis while preserving host antiviral protein production. Next, using an M062-deficient MYXV mutant ({Delta}M062R), we characterized the cellular consequences of unrestricted SAMD9 activation. Unlike vaccinia virus lacking the SAMD9 antagonists C7 and K1 (VACV-{Delta}C7L/K1L), {Delta}M062R infection induced robust ERK1/2 signaling and preserved cell growth despite SAMD9 activation. Meanwhile, {Delta}M062R infection sustained expression of antiviral and proinflammatory proteins while restricting viral protein synthesis. This established a unique cellular state characterized by heightened responsiveness to subsequent innate immune stimulation. These findings identify a previously unrecognized interaction between SAMD9-mediated translation control and ERK1/2 signaling that renders a buffering effect to catastrophic SAMD9-mediated translation shutdown and thus provide new insight into antiviral restriction and innate immune regulation.

title: Two CntT methyltransferases from Actinosynnema mirum and Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal conserved opine-type metallophore methylation but divergent biological roles
content: Opine-type metallophores have been discovered in mono- and diderm bacteria, where they allow zinc import under conditions of severe deficiency, a situation often found in natural environments. Whilst this family of metallophores is relatively well characterised, their modes of action in the organisms in which they are found remain poorly documented. In the present study, we identified and characterized two homologous SAM-dependent methyltransferases from the monoderm Actinosynnema mirum and the diderm Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria. We showed that the corresponding AmCntT (Amir_3913) and PaCntT (PA1921) enzymes methylate their cognate opine-metallophores, staphylopine and pseudopaline, respectively. Crystal structure of AmCntT established key structural features that are unique to this family of methyltransferase, and residues putatively involved in substrate stabilization were probed by site directed mutagenesis. Further investigation showed that, unlike the staphylopine from A. mirum, which is recovered in its methylated form in the extracellular medium, pseudopaline methylation occurred only under certain stress conditions and was only detected for an intracellular pool of pseudopaline, hence suggesting a role in its degradation in P. aeruginosa. Altogether, our data revealed a new common component of the A. mirum and P. aeruginosa opine-metallophore pathways respectively involved in staphylopine and pseudopaline methylation that appears to have distinct functional implications in each organism.

title: Legionella pneumophila DenR is a bacterial S-acyltransferase for the human GTPase NRAS
content: In eukaryotic cells, the covalent attachment of palmitic acid to cysteine residues is catalyzed by the DHHC superfamily of membrane-embedded protein acyltransferases (DHHC-PAT). Here, we discovered that the bacterial pathogen Legionella pneumophila codes for its own protein acyltransferase, DenR, which hijacks host palmitoylation. Unlike the DHHC-PATs, DenR is a cytosolic protein that peripherally associates with membranes via binding of PI3P lipids through its carboxy-terminal domain. PI3P binding allosterically activates the palmitoyltransferase activity of its N-terminal circularly permuted NlpC/P60 papain-like domain, resulting in palmitoylation of the host GTPase NRAS at cysteine 181 and thereby anchoring NRAS to membranes of the Legionella-containing vacuole. Importantly, DenR-mediated S-acylation was insensitive to 2-bromopalmitate treatment, which inhibits cellular protein palmitoylation, suggesting that DenR represents a novel class of cytosolic S-acyltransferase.

title: Cryo-EM-based examinations of honey bee colony losses reveal structural insights into acute bee paralysis virus maturation and mechanical carriage
content: Honey bee colony losses pose a complex and significant agricultural problem in the United States and Europe, which has also been linked to viruses. As opposed to a purely sequence-based approach, we used cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as an alternative sequencing- and culture-independent diagnostic tool to investigate viral pathogens associated with colony losses in the state of Texas. By purifying a limited number of viral particles directly from degraded hive remains, we could establish the identity of acute bee paralysis virus (ABPV) at the species level without prior sequencing data at 3.1 Å resolution, reconstructed of only 443 particles. We showed that small hive beetles carry mature ABPV virions, both within their digestive tract and attached to their cuticle. We successfully utilized cryo- EM to infer active ABPV replication from honey bee carcasses by reconstructing the virion structure of immature provirions at 2.35- and 2.53 [A], respectively, even several days after the collapse, despite the degradation of negative-strand RNA intermediates. Structural characterization of these immature particles revealed that ABPV capsids assemble around a condensed genomic core with the nucleic acid gradually expanding to occupy the capsid interior, ultimately bringing the VP0 structural protein in contact with VP3, which cleaves VP0 to structural proteins VP2 and 4. Together, our findings establish cryo-EM as a complementary diagnostic approach that simultaneously enables viral identification, replication-state assessment, and structural characterization, providing unprecedented insights into the maturation process of aparaviruses, a lineage of honey bee-infecting picorna-like viruses at the forefront of colony losses.

title: A simplified protocol for the generation of apical-out human bladder organoids in suspension using a rotating bioreactor
content: Bladder organoids are commonly generated in extracellular matrix domes, where apical surfaces line an enclosed central lumen, limiting experimental accessibility. Suspension-based systems have been explored to generate polarity-reversed organoids, but current models are often derived from cancer cells, remain incompletely characterized or rely on highly specialized scaffolds. Here, we describe a rapid and scalable approach to generate apical-out human bladder organoids (hBOs) from primary bladder epithelial cells using a rotating bioreactor system with minimal extracellular matrix scaffolding. Organoids form within 8 days and exhibit an apical-out phenotype with outward-facing umbrella-like cells. These apical-out hBOs tolerate 100% pooled human urine for up to 4 hours and can be infected with uropathogenic E. coli, recapitulating hallmarks of infection such as the formation of intracellular bacteria communities. Overall, the apical-out configuration enables direct access to the umbrella cell layer, thereby simplifying experimental manipulation, including infection and treatment assays under physiological conditions.

title: Understanding the dynamics of Telomerase-RNP complex in the human malaria parasite
content: Amongst the human malaria causing species, P. falciparum exhibits an interesting telomere-telomerase (TERT) dynamics. In a striking contrast to humans, which have 10-15 kb long telomeres, parasite telomeres are shorter (1-2 kb) and are maintained by a very large Pf TERT (2.5 times bigger than hTERT) and its structural RNA (Pf TR is 5 times bigger than hTR). Till date, there are no studies on Telomerase-RNP complex in the malaria parasite. The RNP complex comprises of diverged TERT and RNA-interacting proteins (Dyskerin, GAR1, NHP2, NOP10, TCAB1) and structural TR. Interestingly, Pf TR undergoes stage-dependent transcription with non-uniform (heterogeneous) transcript length. The levels of Pf TR transcripts are much higher than that of Pf TERT, suggesting that Pf TR may have scaffolding non-coding RNA roles beyond TERT function. We also observed differential expression of Pf TERT and TR-interacting RNPs with non-stoichiometric cellular abundance. These RNPs can form higher-order complexes, which can be independent of TERT and TR. Through super-resolution microscopy (STORM), we observed distinct perinuclear localization of Pf TERT in ring, trophozoite and schizonts. Genotoxic and oxidative stress conditions affected the expression and subcellular fractionation of plasmodial Telomerase-RNP complex proteins (especially GAR1, NOP10), hinting towards their probable TERT-independent roles. Immunoprecipitation of Telomerase-RNP complex revealed specific enrichment of NOP10 and HSP90, hinting towards variable binding affinities of RNP proteins to Pf TERT. Our results suggest dynamics in the Telomerase-RNP assembly may allow them to perform both canonical and non-canonical functions to support intracellular parasite survival in evolutionary distinct hosts.

title: A 6-week all-liquid caloric restriction diet reduced abundance of some butyrate-producing bacteria while increasing abundance of mucin-degrading bacteria
content: Caloric restriction diets are a common diet strategy to reduce excess weight and obesity. The diets work by lowering the number of calories or energy input below a human's normal energy expenditure creating an energy deficit. Caloric restriction diet meals can be composed of whole foods, meal replacement shakes, or a combination of the two. While the effects of these diets on human metabolism are well-known, the effects of these diets and the durability of these effects on the human gut microbiome are less well-known. The objective of this work was to investigate the effects of a 6-week all-liquid caloric restriction diet on the human gut microbiota using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to assess changes in diversity, community composition, and predicted function. We found that during the diet period beta-diversity shifts significantly away from what it was before the intervention (baseline), and returns to baseline a week after the diet. During the diet period we also observed a decrease in abundance of fiber-degrading and butyrate-producing bacteria with a simultaneous increase in abundance of mucin-degrading bacteria with a return to baseline level abundances in the post-diet period. Despite a liquid diet relatively high in carbohydrate (59% carbohydrate, 25% fat, 16% protein), predicted function analysis showed a shift in substrate preference away from dietary carbohydrates towards protein and host-glycans during the diet period. These findings suggest that despite the overall high carbohydrate content all-liquid caloric restriction diets deprive the gut microbiota of their preferred nutrient source due to the overall decline in calorie delivery which forces them to consume alternative nutrient sources like protein and host-glycans.

title: Rapid development of E. coli resistance to Bdellovibrio predation during short-term co-culture
content: When E. coli ML35 is co-cultured with Bdellovibrio sp. NC01 over 72 hours, prey populations initially experience a 3-log reduction, but then partially recover to ~20% of starting density. Population recovery is correlated with emergence of irregular colonies, which are distinct from typical circular ML35 morphotype. ML35 populations do not recover when co-cultured with Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus HD100, and irregular colonies are not observed in HD100 co-cultures or in prey-only controls. Whole-genome sequencing of clonal lines of irregular and circular morphotypes from three independent replicate assays confirmed they are derived from ML35. ML35-irregular is resistant to killing by Bdellovibrio sp. NC01 but susceptible to killing by HD100, indicating strain-specific predation resistance. Analysis of sequencing data showed that all three ML35-irregular lines and all three ML35-circular lines carry a mutation in rfbG, annotated as dTDP-rhamnosyl transferase involved in O-antigen synthesis. Two ML35-irregular lines have distinct IS element insertions in rfbG; the third has a substitution introducing a premature stop codon near the C-terminus. Two ML35-circular lines have the same missense mutation in rfbG, whereas the third has a nonstop mutation. Overall, these data suggest that rfbG may be under selective pressure during NC01 co-culture and that O-antigen may play a role in predation resistance. Further work, such as phenotypic testing of ML35-circular lines and reverse genetics experiments, are needed to clarify how rfbG affects prey susceptibility to Bdellovibrio predation.

title: Characterizing the Effects of Filtration on Microbial Diversity, Reproducibility, and Genome Recovery from Wastewater
content: Filtration is widely used in wastewater microbiome workflows, but how pore size, filtration tactics, and sampled fraction shape microbial profiles across sequencing approaches remains unclear. We compared direct and sequential filtration of wastewater through 3-, 0.45-, and 0.22- micro meter filters and analyzed filter-retained and corresponding filtrates using 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and metatranscriptomics. Filtrates generally yielded higher microbial alpha diversity but greater between-replicate variability, whereas filters produced more reproducible bacterial DNA profiles. Fraction-dependent differences were strongest for fungal and DNA viral communities, which separated between filters and filtrates, while bacterial DNA communities were largely shared across fractions. These patterns demonstrate that pore size does not act as a strict size cutoff in wastewater for bacteria. DNA viruses were consistently enriched in filtrates, which also yielded more viral genomes. In contrast, filters yielded more bacterial metagenome-assembled genomes, but overall bacterial genome recovery was limited. Bacterial and viral metatranscriptomic profiles were comparatively variable and did not support selection of a single preferred fraction for RNA-based recovery. Direct and sequential filtration also produced distinct profiles at the same terminal pore size, indicating that filtration history influences the recovered community. Together, these results suggest that wastewater processing workflow should therefore be selected according to the intended use case.

title: A multi-scale forecasting framework to prioritize clinically-relevant antibiotic resistance alleles
content: Established in vitro measures for the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, a critical global threat, can fail to predict which in vitro discovered mutations will dominate in the real world following widespread antibiotic use. Here, we introduce a multi-scale computational framework integrating genetic constraints and population pharmacokinetics and apply it to explain resistance allele success in Acinetobacter baumannii for the historic case of resistance to the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin. By coupling intrinsic nucleotide substitution likelihoods with continuous-time stochastic modeling under fluctuating drug exposures, our framework clearly prioritizes the most common real world gyrA fluoroquinolone resistance allele S81L over rarer alleles, reflecting its clinical success. While gyrA serves as a proof-of-concept case study for direct, active-site drug-target interactions where the target space is constrained, we observe that the nucleotide substitution likelihoods are not explaining allele success in resistance-determining genes pmrB and adeS. Furthermore, "virtual twin" cohort simulations reveal that restricted drug penetration or compromised immunity expands selective windows, rescuing rare, low-fitness alleles. This advances our understanding of prospective, model-informed risk prediction during antibiotic development.

title: Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., novel taxa isolated from figs (Ficus)
content: Two bacterial strains, WOUb02T and WOUb67T, were isolated from fresh figs (Ficus spp.) collected from the island of Taiwan. Cells of WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Gram-stain-negative rods. Strain WOUb02T was non-motile, whereas WOUb67T exhibited motility. Physiologically, both strains grew optimally at 0.5% (w/v) NaCl and pH 8.0; WOUb02T grew optimally at 37{degrees}C, whereas WOUb67T grew optimally at 30{degrees}C. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the closest relatives to strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Klebsiella terrigena ATCC 33257T (98.2%) and Pseudomonas putida NBRC 14164T (99.9%) respectively. Subsequent phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T formed distinct lineages within the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively. Further genomic analyses revealed that WOUb02T and WOUb67T shared average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values <95.0% and <70.0%, below the currently accepted thresholds for species-level delineation. Based on phenotypic and genotypic data, strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T could be distinguished from other species with validly published names and are considered to represent novel species in the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively, for which the names Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., are proposed. The type strains are WOUb02T (=NRRL-B 65719T =CCUG 77855T) and WOUb67T (=NRRL-B 65720T =CCUG 77856T).

title: Species turnover dominates plant trait variation along continental climate gradients
content: Variation in plant functional traits along climate gradients chiefly arises from two processes: turnover of species with different trait values, and trait adjustment within species across environments. Yet, the relative contributions of these processes remain poorly quantified, limiting our ability to predict how traits, species distributions and, in turn, ecosystem properties will respond to climate change. Across seven functional traits and 1867 plant taxa from continental Australia, we provide a unified assessment of among- versus within-species contributions across multiple dimensions of plant function. Species turnover emerged as the dominant process driving trait variation along both precipitation and temperature gradients. Nevertheless, the contribution of within-species adjustment to climate differed substantially among traits and was generally greater in non-woody than woody taxa, these patterns being most clearly expressed along precipitation gradients. Our findings imply that plant traits will track changing climatic conditions primarily through species replacement, particularly for traits such as wood density and seed mass. Species may also respond in situ through adjustments in leaf physiology and morphology and, in woody taxa, through shifts in relative allocation between leaves and stem tissues. This knowledge has potential to improve predictions of the structure and function of future plant communities.

title: Historical overestimated abundance of a Critically Endangered species: the case of the tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) of Mindoro Island
content: Population abundance is a central parameter in conservation, for which biased estimates can seriously undermine management strategies for threatened species. The tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) is a Critically Endangered large herbivore endemic to Mindoro Island, Philippines. The species has been monitored annually at Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park (MIBNP) since 2000 using a multi-vantage-point count method that is prone to both imperfect detection and repeated counting of the same individuals across sessions. Because the historical abundance estimation is an index of relative abundance with no probabilistic modeling of counts, the actual number of tamaraw in what is considered as the largest remaining population is still poorly known. To fill this gap, we conducted an independent double-observer experiment over five years (2022-2026) and fitted Bayesian hierarchical detection models to the counts. As expected, detection probability was <1 throughout (single-observer estimates 0.41-0.84; combined-observer 0.68-0.96), confirming that a substantial fraction of animals is missed by rangers during all counts. Compared with these estimates, historical counts overestimated tamaraw abundance by a factor of 1.61-2.34, yielding a mean population size across 2022-2026 of 203 individuals (95% credible interval 182-226) rather than the roughly 400-500 individuals previously assumed. Our results imply that the MIBNP tamaraw population, while more vulnerable to demographic and genetic risks than previously believed, has likely responded positively to ongoing conservation efforts; we recommend that population viability assessments and translocation plans for the species be revised accordingly.

title: Apple floral attractants function across the 24-hour cycle to support potential diurnal and nocturnal pollinators
content: Pollination in apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is typically attributed to diurnal bees, yet nocturnal insects also contribute to fruit set. To assess whether apple flowers recruit potential pollinators throughout the 24-hour cycle, we quantified diel patterns in floral attractants and insect visitation in an orchard in Northwest Arkansas, United States. We measured nectar and volatiles and used a combination of visual surveys, light traps, and video recordings to assess insect abundance and floral visitation while controlling for weather conditions. We found that nectar volume remained consistent across sampling times, indicating that reward availability is dielly stable. Floral volatile bouquets, in contrast, exhibited subtle but significant diel and interannual variation, driven largely by shifts in aldehydes, alkanes, and benzenoids. Several compounds associated with nocturnal moth and dipteran attraction - including alpha-farnesene, benzyl alcohol, and aldehydes - were enriched at night. Apple flowers were visited by insects around the clock. Nighttime visitors were less abundant than daytime visitors but taxonomically diverse, including moths and nematoceran flies, whereas bees, wasps, and brachyceran flies were restricted to daytime. Different taxonomic groups therefore alternated over the diel cycle, producing pronounced shifts in visitor community composition. Thus, apple flowers produce attractants across the diel cycle and nocturnal insects - particularly dipterans and moths - are a consistent, ecologically meaningful component of the apple flower-visiting assemblage. Our findings support the need for pollinator-inclusive management that accounts for the full diel cycle, particularly when scheduling pesticide applications near bloom, to sustain diverse pollinator communities and enhance the resilience of apple production systems.

title: The use of cultured symbionts enhances the survival of reef-deployed coral recruits
content: Introduction: Symbiodiniaceae dinoflagellates are essential for coral juvenile development and survival, yet early-life symbiont provisioning remains underused in coral restoration. Objectives: We tested whether inoculating sexually propagated Acropora spathulata recruits with cultured symbionts before reef deployment improves survival and shapes symbiont community composition. Methods: Recruits inoculated with cultured Cladocopium sp. (C1) or Durusdinium trenchii (D1), and uninoculated recruits (Control) were deployed on the central Great Barrier Reef. Results: Both inoculation treatments approximately doubled survival relative to Control, although the benefit varied with local benthic habitat. C1 and D1 recruits were dominated by symbiont sequences matching their respective inoculated cultures, while Control recruits predominantly harboured a Durusdinium-dominant community closely resembling the cultured D1. Cultured C1 was also dominant among most C1-inoculated recruits after nine months, although some diverged from the inoculated community towards a mixed assemblage with Durusdinium. Conclusions: Similar survival benefits in the two inoculation treatments suggest that the timing and success of symbiont establishment were more critical for early survival than symbiont genus identity, under the conditions and period of this study.

title: Differential population declines across migratory strategies are shifting European bird communities towards residency
content: Previous studies revealed steep declines in populations of common migratory birds across Europe, especially for long-distance migrants. However, these studies focussed on continental-scale patterns, and they assigned a single migratory strategy to each species, often not distinguishing short-distance migrants from residents. It thus remains unclear whether the same patterns are found across European countries, and whether they hold when taking into account the variation in migratory behaviour observed across the European populations of many species. Here, we examine how European breeding landbird communities have varied according to migratory strategy between 1990 and 2023, at both continental and national scales. By compiling multiple sources of information on seasonal movements, we characterise the migratory strategy of landbird populations per country (long-distance migrant, short-distance migrant or resident). We combined these data with estimates of population trends and of abundance from national monitoring schemes to quantify changes in both multi-species indices (average change across species) and total abundance of birds, for each migratory strategy. At the continental scale, multi-species indices reveal a strong decline in long-distance migrants (-26.8% between 1990 and 2023), whereas short-distance migrants declined more slowly (-4.5%) and residents remained stable. Changes in total abundance show even steeper declines - of 29.9% and 10.2% for, respectively, long- and short-distance migrants - whereas residents increased slightly (+3.4%). Together, these results point to a gradual reorganisation of bird communities towards a greater dominance of resident birds across Europe. However, these changes are not happening homogenously across the continent: whereas in Central and Southern Europe we observed the same general pattern of declining migrants while residents remained broadly stable or increased, in Northern Europe we reveal declines for all migratory strategies. Overall, our study highlights the widespread vulnerability of migratory birds in Europe, while showing that the reorganisation of bird communities follows different trajectories across regions.

title: Normalised whole-plant water supply declines with plant height across the seed-plant phylogeny
content: Whole-plant water-transport capacity largely controls terrestrial water fluxes, yet it is unresolved to what extent its variation across the seed-plant phylogeny is structured by shared ancestry, edaphoclimatic conditions, plant height or water relation traits. We fitted a phylogenetic structural equation model to maximum leaf-specific whole-plant hydraulic conductance (kL), together with concurrent Huber value (Hv), stomatal conductance (gs), and height for 263 species spanning the global climate space, partitioning direct from indirect effects, and phylogenetically conserved from independent effects. kL declined with height, and Hv did not offset this decline. Hv raised kL but was unrelated to height among species. kL was lower in wetter niches, despite higher Hv there, indicating lower conductance per unit sapwood area. kL was tightly coupled to gs in both conserved and independent variation, so the height-driven decline in kL propagated to gas exchange. Plant height therefore constrains whole-plant hydraulic supply and, through it, gs.
